title: Brush PETG residue off a Prusa MK4S heater block before printing robot parts, keeping the brass brush off its leads
instruction: Brush the PETG residue off the heater block's underside with the brass brush, leaving the tray in place; then lay the brush back on the counter and clear both hands.
context: Builders of the Upkie wheeled biped print its PETG femurs, tibias, wheel hubs and torso plates on a Prusa printer; its guide uses an MK3S+ and says other printers work with the same settings. Prusa's MK4S guide says to check the hotend before every print: heat it to 250 C, brush old plastic off the nozzle and heater block with a brass brush so it cannot fall onto the part, and keep the brush off the hotend cables. This task is that check before the next robot part is printed.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the counter. Original Prusa MK4S (500 x 550 x 400, 7 kg), switched off right after the 250 C pre-heat, fixed, front facing the arms, centred at x 305, y 0; build plate top 100 up. Its carriage is parked with the nozzle tip at (270, 0, 170). Heater block 13 x 20 x 12 (estimate), turned 35 degrees, centre (270, 0, 182); brass nozzle shows 6 below it (8 across at the shoulder, 1.2 at the tip). The fan shroud walls stand 25 either side of the block and 27 behind it; the front is open. Two red heater leads (2.2 across) and two white thermistor leads (1.3 across) leave the block's back left face square to it at the block's mid-height (lowest point 4.9 above the underside), 4 to 9 left of the face's centre line, run 12 out and turn up. Residue: one standard dark PETG coupon, 0.2 thick, bonded to the block underside during the pre-heat; it covers the underside to 0.5 from its edges except a 3 wide bare strip along the lead-exit face and a 4.5 radius hole round the nozzle (120 mm2; fixture drawing). Prusa Brass Nozzle Brush: beech handle and head 172 x 12 x 12, 14 mm brass bristles on a 34 mm head, 35 g (sizes estimated); lies bristles up along x, handle end at x 170, head end at x 342, centred on y 265. Stainless catch tray 120 x 80 x 15 (1 mm sheet, 140 g estimate), loose on the plate, centred at (250, -10). Lot B: brush handle end at x 90 (head end 262), y 255; tray centred at (290, 10). Both lots are run and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. The standard Nextruder sock is removed to expose the block; its public listing rates it to 300 C (README link), distinct from the finger-cover sheet. All four fingers carry a 1/16 in (1.5875 mm) USA Industrials BULK-RS-S50FDA-226 high-temperature silicone cover over each distal pad and tip. Material and adhesive are rated 260 C. Before first use, the assessor enrols the covers on a spare finger: a thermocouple at the pad interface during a timed touch on the 250 C block must stay below the pad maker's limit; covers are replaced after any touch. Covers have matching collision geometry and estimated 0.9/0.8 static/sliding wood friction in simulation. Proposed real-trial kit, about US$390: a replica carriage with a ready-assembled Nextruder hotend, the MK4S fan shroud and full-size frame obstacles, build plate, two brass brushes, tray, 24 V supply and controller, USB microscope, coupon transfer stand on a lab jack, Prusament PETG and the finger covers (README lists parts, prices and checks).
scoring: Read from the overhead and wrist videos, a 60 fps close video of the lead exit, before and after photos of the block underside (USB microscope with a mirror, 0.05 mm per pixel or finer, scale in view, the coupon outline overlaid) and a ruler. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment: any part of the brush, bristles included, touches a heater or thermistor lead (close video; a talc dusting on the leads shows any touch); a robot finger touches the hot block or nozzle (wrist and close video; the assessor stops the trial; the simulation counts 3 mm as touching); the brush's wood touches the block or nozzle (a chalk line along the head's top edges shows it); or the brush or tray falls off the counter. Otherwise measure the share of the coupon outline left bare in the after photo (dark film thresholded on the photo); film pushed elsewhere inside the outline, into the 3 mm lead strip or onto a lead still counts as present: 1.0 for 95% or more cleared; 0.75 for 80% to under 95%; 0.5 for 50% to under 80%; 0.25 for 25% to under 50%; 0 below 25%. Every score above 0 needs, for the last 2 s: the brush lying on the counter to the left of the printer (y over 225), released; the tray on the build plate, upright within 5 degrees, its bottom within 2 mm of the plate and the nozzle axis at least 8 mm inside each floor edge; both hands at least 30 mm from the brush, tray, block and nozzle; and nothing moving more than 1 mm. Lots A and B are averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: Reset about 10.5 min per accepted preparation, including batch share. Heat-up (20 to 250 C) 70 s, extrusion (30 mm) 12 s, coupon press 8 s: figures obtained by phone from a technician who works with this product (Nov 2026). Other times are estimates. Replica: hand-feed marked filament through the cold heatsink inlet; 12 s is a planning allocation from the MK4S figure, not a replica measurement. 1. After photo (1 min). 2. Heat to 250 C (70 s), hold 3 min per maker, hand-brush old film (1 min). 3. Extrude 30 mm (12 s), remove purge strand, load coupon on PTFE platen, align 9 mm hole, raise jack, press onto block (8 s); lower below nozzle tip and withdraw (0.5 min handling). 4. Enrol with calibrated underside photo: film covers >=95% of outline, none in lead strip or on leads; reject and repeat steps 2-4 otherwise (1 min photo). 5. Empty tray, wipe plate, renew witness marks, inspect covers, restore lot marks (1 min). 6. Switch heater off; start within 30 s (0.5 min). Batch estimate: 24 coupons in 25 min including slicing, heat-up, printing, cooling/removal (62.5 s/trial). Add actual rejected-prep, repair and cover-replacement time; no fixed upper bound. Transfer/bond repeatability and full reset remain unmeasured. New covers need spare-pad thermal qualification. Simulation restores coupon and lot.
fidelity: Full-size printer reconstruction; hotend/lead sizes estimated. Free brush feels 27 ray tufts (14 mm, 25 N/m estimated from wire bending); fixed printer supports the reaction. 482 cells (0.5 mm) clear under >=1.5 mm tuft bend and >=4 mm slide away from leads. Lead overlap/wood within 0.1 mm/fingers within 3 mm latch 0. Cover colliders add 1.5875 mm; wood friction 0.9/0.8 estimated. Heat, cooling, PETG flow, cover compliance/mass and pad insulation are unmodelled. Removal loads are unmeasured.
scores: Scripted demo A 1.0/B 1.0 (482/482; 481/482 cells). Dream-1 A 0.0/B 0.0: both hit the 2400-step limit with no residue removed; 40 expired provider requests were retried, no evaluation errors. Same revised source, two lots.
